customManagers.description: The Angular CLI installed globally in the debug image
The dotnet-ef tool the backend image uses to build the migrations bundle. semver versioning, because NuGet versioning reads a bare 10.0.0 as the range >= 10.0.0 and never offers an update

The .NET images (Dockerfile FROM ...:10.0-alpine), looked up in .NET's own release list rather than the image tags: the tags exist from the first preview, the list has a stable 11.0.x only once 11.0 ships (previews like 11.0.0-rc.2 don't match extractVersion). The docker manager's own lookup of these images is off (packageRules)
The projects' TargetFramework (net10.0), moved with the images in the .NET major PR
The SDK the .NET tests install (DOTNET_VERSION: 10.0.x in dotnet-tests.yml)

packageRules.description: Everything goes into one PR, majors included

Everything tied to the Angular version gets its own PR, never the big one: Angular itself, Node (the client build images and the CI setup-node versions), the CLI in debug.Dockerfile (@angular/cli, the custom manager above), and @material/material-color-utilities (the theme service builds the M3 palettes with it). Minors and patches go to an Angular PR (renovate/angular), majors to Angular major (renovate/major-angular, below)
Packages tied to the .NET version: keep minors in the big PR but split majors out
NetCord (the Discord library) gets its own PR: it is a prerelease, and each new one can break the bot
The brackets libraries (brackets-manager, brackets-model, brackets-viewer) get their own PR: they make and draw the event brackets, and move together

Angular majors get their own PR; they need ng update migrations and careful testing. @angular/material and @angular/cdk are covered by @angular/**; the @ng-matero libraries and ngx-drag-drop release one major per Angular major, so they ride along
zone.js is 0.x and each minor pairs with an Angular major; the slug makes its minor land in the same renovate/major-angular branch as the Angular majors
Node (the client build images and the CI setup-node versions, which Renovate looks up as actions/node-versions) must be a version the Angular CLI supports
Angular only supports one TypeScript minor at a time and ng update bumps it during Angular majors, so Renovate only does TypeScript patches

.NET majors get their own PR: the projects' TargetFramework (net10.0) has to move with them, which Renovate can't do. AspNet.Security.OAuth.* and the Serilog hosting/configuration bridges are versioned with .NET; dotnet-ef must match EF Core; dotnet-sdk is the CI setup-dotnet version
The .NET images are looked up by the regex manager above (.NET's release list), not by their tags, which offer a .NET major from its first preview

Tailwind CSS majors get their own PR: they change the configuration and the PostCSS plugin (4.0 moved it to @tailwindcss/postcss), so they need a migration (npx @tailwindcss/upgrade). Minors and patches stay in the big PR

NUnit majors get their own PR: they change the assertion API (5.0: Assert.ThrowsAsync returns a Task to await), so the tests need fixing with them. NUnit3TestAdapter and NUnit.Analyzers majors come along. Minors and patches stay in the big PR
